questions.question_hindi:

II. निर्णय-पैकेज तैयार करना।
III. निर्णय-पैकेजों की प्राथमिकता तय करना।
IV. प्राथमिकता के अनुसार संसाधन आवंटित करना। सही क्रम क्या है?
options_hindi: I, II, III, IV
II, I, III, IV
I, III, II, IV
III, II, I, IV
questions.question_english: Review the following steps in the Zero-Based Budgeting process: I. Identification of decision units. II. Preparation of decision packages. III. Ranking of decision packages. IV. Allocation of resources based on the ranking. What is the correct sequential order of these steps?
options_english: I, II, III, IV
II, I, III, IV
I, III, II, IV
III, II, I, IV
questions.explanation_english: I, II, III, IV. The standard procedure in Zero-Based Budgeting follows a logical four-step sequence. First, organizational activities are divided into distinct decision units. Second, comprehensive decision packages detailing costs and benefits are prepared for each unit. Third, managers evaluate and rank these packages based on strategic priorities. Finally, available financial resources are allocated according to the finalized rankings
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। ZBB में पहले निर्णय इकाइयाँ पहचानी जाती हैं, फिर निर्णय-पैकेज बनाए और क्रमबद्ध किए जाते हैं, और उसके बाद प्राथमिकताओं के आधार पर संसाधन बाँटे जाते हैं।
key_facts: Answer key: (A)

questions.question_english: Revenue Expenditure in a school budget is primarily characterized by:
options_english: Financial outlay resulting in the creation of new, long-term physical assets and structural additions for the school
Substantial capital investments made for acquiring new land parcels for future school expansion and development
Long-term loans and financial advances granted by the institution to other government departments or agencies
Recurring expenses necessary for normal day-to-day functioning
questions.explanation_english: Recurring expenses necessary for normal day-to-day functioning. Revenue Expenditure in institutional budgeting covers recurring, short-term operational costs essential for continuous day-to-day operations. Unlike capital spending, revenue expenditure does not create permanent physical assets or reduce financial liabilities. It includes regular establishment costs, staff salaries, utility bills, administrative contingencies, minor maintenance repairs, and consumable classroom supplies
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। राजस्व व्यय वे बार-बार होने वाले खर्च हैं जो विद्यालय के सामान्य दैनिक संचालन के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं; वे सामान्यतः नई दीर्घकालिक परिसंपत्ति नहीं बनाते।

questions.question_english: Consider the two statements below: Assertion (A) and Reason (R): Assertion (A): Zero-Based Budgeting prevents the automatic continuation of obsolete educational programs from one financial year to the next. Reason (R): Under ZBB, the historical spending levels are considered the minimum baseline for the new budget, ensuring continuity.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: A is true but R is false. Zero-Based Budgeting effectively prevents the automatic continuation of obsolete programs by requiring fresh justification for every activity during each budget cycle. However, the reasoning provided is false because ZBB completely rejects historical spending as a mandatory baseline. Instead of assuming past allocations as given, ZBB starts from a zero base, eliminating unjustified recurring expenses

key_facts: Answer key: (C)

options_english: Project the entire ₹50 Lakhs as savings to be re-appropriated or surrendered
Hide the construction delay and transfer the ₹50 Lakhs to the SMC account to prevent funds from lapsing

questions.question_english: An internal audit team discovers that the school’s Cash Book has not been closed and signed by the Principal for three months. What is the immediate expected action?

Lock the Cash Book in a safe and refuse to present it to external audit officials
Allow the internal audit inspection team to confiscate the Cash Book permanently

questions.explanation_english: Update entries, reconcile balance, sign Cash Book, and ensure daily closing. When an internal audit team identifies an unclosed Cash Book, the Principal must take immediate corrective action. The DDO should immediately update all missing financial entries, reconcile bank and treasury balances, sign the Cash Book, and enforce mandatory daily closing procedures to maintain statutory accounting compliance in the future

questions.question_english: Select the statement that is incorrect regarding Revised Estimates (RE):

questions.explanation_english: It acts as authorization to spend additional funds without supplementary grants. questions.question_english: A Principal placed an order for dual desks on GeM in January. By March 15th, the supplier cancels the order, and it is impossible to initiate a new procurement before March 31st. What is the mandatory financial action required?
options_english: Surrender the unutilized amount to the government immediately
Retain the allocated funds safely in the school’s bank account for procurement during the next financial year
Issue an official treasury cheque to the vendor before March 31st and request them to deliver goods next year
Distribute the remaining allocated money equally among the SMC members to conduct local market purchases
questions.explanation_english: Surrender the unutilized amount to the government immediately. When a GeM supplier cancels an order in mid- March and fresh procurement is impossible before March 31st, the allocated funds cannot be spent legally. The Principal must surrender the unutilized amount to the government immediately. Retaining funds illegally, post- dating cheques, or distributing money to committee members constitutes severe financial violations
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। जब मार्च के अंत से पहले सामान लेना संभव न हो, तो अप्रयुक्त राशि को रोके रखने या काल्पनिक भुगतान करने के बजाय सरकार को समर्पित करना चाहिए।

questions.question_english: Review the following characteristics: I. It results in the creation of an asset that will yield benefits in future years. II. It is recurring in nature and occurs every month. III. It usually involves a substantial financial outlay compared to routine expenses. Which of the characteristics given above correctly describe Capital Expenditure?
options_english: I and II only
I and III only
II and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: I and III only. Capital Expenditure is defined by long-term institutional benefits through asset creation and typically involves substantial financial outlay compared to routine expenses. Statement II is incorrect because capital spending is non- recurring rather than occurring monthly. Recurring monthly expenses belong to revenue expenditure. Therefore, characteristics I and III correctly describe Capital Expenditure
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। पूंजीगत व्यय से भविष्य में लाभ देने वाली परिसंपत्ति बनती है और इसमें अक्सर बड़ी प्रारंभिक राशि लगती है; हर महीने दोहराया जाना इसकी विशेषता नहीं है।
key_facts: Answer key: (B)
